records.source: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος· καὶ καθίσαντος αὐτοῦ προσῆλθαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: Having seen then the crowds he went up into the mountain; and having sat down of him came to him the disciples of him;
pieces: Seeing the crowds, Jesus went up onto the mountain. He sat down, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.1: And seeing the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up on the mountain, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had sat down, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},

R.1: Jesus saw the crowds of people, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up on a hill and sat down. His followers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: went up on the mountain: perhaps an echo of Moses on Sinai
alternatives: only a place where the crowd could hear
decisions.reason: Moses went up the mountain to receive the law (Exodus 19:3). Here Jesus goes up a mountain and teaches what the law means (5:17-48). Matthew does not name the mountain or draw the comparison.

decisions.choice: sat down: the posture of a teacher
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers sat to teach (23:2; Luke 4:20).

decisions.choice: his disciples, with the crowds also listening
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to his disciples, but at the end the crowds are amazed at his teaching (7:28-29).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: followers
decisions.reason: Readable says what disciples are.

records.heading: The Sermon on the Mount

records.source: καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς λέγων·
records.gloss: And having opened the mouth of him he was teaching them saying:
pieces: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach them:

L.2: and opening {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them, saying:

R.2: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach them. He said:

decisions.choice: opening his mouth: a solemn way to begin an important speech
decisions.reason: The phrase marks what follows as weighty teaching (compare Job 3:1; Acts 8:35).

decisions.choice: began to teach them
alternatives: opened his mouth and taught them
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures the teaching under way. Balanced and Readable say he began, and leave out the idiom, which the meaning note explains.

records.source: Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
records.gloss: Blessed the poor in the spirit, for of them is the kingdom of the heavens.
pieces: "Blessed are those who are poor in spirit: the kingdom of heaven is theirs.

L.3: "Blessed [are] the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.

R.3: "Blessed are those who know they are poor and need God. The kingdom of heaven belongs to them.

decisions.choice: blessed: in the happy state of those God favors
alternatives: may they be blessed, as a wish
decisions.reason: The word describes people who are well off in God's eyes, whatever they feel. Each saying states a fact about them and gives the reason in what God will do. The form is known from the Psalms and Proverbs (Psalm 1:1; 32:1).

decisions.choice: poor in spirit: those who know they have nothing to offer God and depend on him
decisions.reason: In the Psalms and Isaiah the poor are the humble who look to God for help (Psalm 34:7, 19; Isaiah 61:1; 66:2). "In spirit" makes clear that an inner poverty is meant, though Jesus's hearers included many who were poor in fact.

decisions.choice: theirs is the kingdom: the first and last sayings promise the kingdom now
decisions.reason: The first saying and the eighth (5:10) both have "is"; the six between have "will". The kingdom frames the list, and its blessings are both present and to come.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: those who know they are poor and need God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase.

records.source: μακάριοι οἱ πενθοῦντες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ παρακληθήσονται.
records.gloss: Blessed the mourning, for they will be comforted.
pieces: Blessed are those who mourn: they will be comforted.

L.4: Blessed [are] those who mourn, for they will be comforted.

R.4: Blessed are those who are sad and grieving. God will comfort them.

decisions.choice: those who mourn ... will be comforted: an echo of Isaiah 61:2
alternatives: grief of any kind with no echo
decisions.reason: Isaiah 61:1-3 promises good news to the poor and comfort to all who mourn, the mourners of Zion. Jesus's words recall that promise; the mourning includes grief over sin and over the state of God's people.

decisions.choice: will be comforted: God is the one who will do it
decisions.reason: Jewish speech often used the passive to speak of what God does without naming him. Readable names God.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: God will comfort them
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the passive implies.

records.source: μακάριοι οἱ πραεῖς, ὅτι αὐτοὶ κληρονομήσουσι τὴν γῆν.
records.gloss: Blessed the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
pieces: Blessed are the gentle: they will inherit the earth.

L.5: Blessed [are] the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

R.5: Blessed are those who are gentle and humble. God will give them the earth as their own.

decisions.choice: the meek will inherit the earth: Psalm 37:11
decisions.reason: Psalm 37:11 says that the meek will inherit the land. There the land is Israel's promised land; Jesus widens it to the whole earth renewed (19:28).

decisions.choice: meek: gentle and humble, not grasping or violent
decisions.reason: The word describes those who do not push for their own way and leave their cause with God. Jesus uses it of himself (11:29; 21:5).

decisions.choice: the earth
decisions.reason: The same word means land or earth. In the psalm it is the land; here, in a saying addressed to all disciples, the wider sense fits.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: gentle (B); gentle and humble (R)
decisions.reason: "Meek" can now suggest weakness. Balanced and Readable use words for the quality meant.

records.source: μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες καὶ διψῶντες τὴν δικαιοσύνην, ὅτι αὐτοὶ χορτασθήσονται.
records.gloss: Blessed the hungering and thirsting [for] the righteousness, for they will be filled.
pieces: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness: they will be satisfied.

L.6: Blessed [are] those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.

R.6: Blessed are those who long for righteousness the way a hungry person longs for food and a thirsty person for water. God will give them all they long for.

decisions.choice: righteousness: right living before God, and God setting things right
decisions.reason: In Matthew righteousness is doing God's will (5:10, 20; 6:1, 33). Those who long for it want to live rightly and want God's justice in the world. Both are in view.

decisions.choice: will be filled: God is the one who will do it
decisions.reason: Jewish speech often used the passive to speak of what God does without naming him. Readable names God.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: the way a hungry person longs for food; God will give them all they long for
alternatives: hunger and thirst for; will be filled
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture and names God.

records.source: μακάριοι οἱ ἐλεήμονες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἐλεηθήσονται.
records.gloss: Blessed the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
pieces: Blessed are the merciful: mercy will be shown to them.

L.7: Blessed [are] the merciful, for they will receive mercy.

R.7: Blessed are those who show mercy to others. God will show mercy to them.

decisions.choice: the merciful will receive mercy: from God, at the judgment
decisions.reason: Matthew links mercy given and mercy received (6:12, 14-15; 18:33). The passive points to God.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: God will show mercy to them
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the passive implies.

records.source: μακάριοι οἱ καθαροὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, ὅτι αὐτοὶ τὸν θεὸν ὄψονται.
records.gloss: Blessed the pure in the heart, for they the God will see.
pieces: Blessed are the pure in heart: they will see God.

L.8: Blessed [are] the pure in heart, for they will see God.

R.8: Blessed are those whose hearts are pure. They will see God.

decisions.choice: pure in heart: undivided in devotion to God (Psalm 24:3-4)
decisions.reason: Psalm 24 asks who may stand in God's presence and answers: those with clean hands and a pure heart. The heart is the whole inner person.

decisions.choice: will see God: be in his presence
decisions.reason: Seeing God is the hope of being with him (Psalm 17:15; Revelation 22:4).

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

records.source: μακάριοι οἱ εἰρηνοποιοί, ὅτι αὐτοὶ υἱοὶ θεοῦ κληθήσονται.
records.gloss: Blessed the peacemakers, for they sons of God will be called.
pieces: Blessed are those who make peace: they will be called {{gender:children|sons}} of God.

L.9: Blessed [are] the peacemakers, for they will be called {{gender:children|sons}} of God.

R.9: Blessed are those who work to bring peace. God will call them {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{gender:children|sons}}.

decisions.choice: peacemakers: those who make peace between people
decisions.reason: The word is active: people who bring about peace where there is quarrel and hatred (5:23-24, 44).

decisions.choice: called sons of God: God will own them as his children
decisions.reason: "Son of" describes likeness and belonging; those who make peace are like the God of peace (5:45). The word includes all of them, men and women.

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The inclusive default says who is meant; the traditional form keeps "sons".

records.source: μακάριοι οἱ δεδιωγμένοι ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
records.gloss: Blessed the having been persecuted on account of righteousness, for of them is the kingdom of the heavens.
pieces: Blessed are those who suffer persecution for the sake of righteousness: the kingdom of heaven is theirs.

L.10: Blessed [are] those who have been persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.

R.10: Blessed are those who are treated badly because they do what is righteous. The kingdom of heaven belongs to them.

decisions.choice: for the sake of righteousness: because they do what God requires
decisions.reason: They suffer for living rightly, as in 5:6. The next saying makes the cause Jesus himself (5:11).

decisions.choice: theirs is the kingdom: the same promise as the first saying
decisions.reason: The repetition closes the eight sayings (see 5:3).

decisions.choice: Blessed are ...: the promise after a colon
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps each saying in two halves, the blessing and the promise, and lets the colon stand for the Greek "for". Literal keeps "for".

records.source: μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν ὀνειδίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ διώξωσιν καὶ εἴπωσιν πᾶν πονηρὸν καθ’ ὑμῶν ψευδόμενοι ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ.
records.gloss: Blessed are you when they insult you and persecute and say every evil against you lying on account of me.
pieces: You are blessed when people abuse you and persecute you and spread all sorts of evil lies about you for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake.

L.11: Blessed are you when they insult you and persecute [you] and say every evil [thing] against you, lying, because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.11: You are blessed when people say bad things about you and hurt you and tell lies about you because you follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: blessed are you: Jesus now speaks to his hearers directly
alternatives: a ninth blessing like the others
decisions.reason: The sayings change from "those who" to "you", and the cause becomes loyalty to Jesus.

decisions.choice: lying: what they say about you is false
decisions.reason: The word limits the blessing: it is for those who are slandered falsely.

decisions.choice: because you follow me
decisions.reason: Readable says why they are treated this way.

records.source: χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, ὅτι ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· οὕτως γὰρ ἐδίωξαν τοὺς προφήτας τοὺς πρὸ ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: Rejoice and be glad, for the reward of you [is] great in the heavens; thus for they persecuted the prophets the before you.
pieces: Rejoice and celebrate, because a great reward is waiting for you in heaven. That is how they persecuted the prophets who came before you.

L.12: Rejoice and be glad, for your reward [is] great in the heavens, for in this way they persecuted the prophets who [were] before you.

R.12: Be happy and celebrate! You will have a great reward in heaven. People treated the prophets who lived before you in the same way.

decisions.choice: your reward in heaven: what God has kept for you
decisions.reason: Heaven here is where God keeps what he will give (6:20). The reward is his gift, not wages.

decisions.choice: the prophets before you: those whom Israel rejected and persecuted
decisions.reason: Jeremiah was beaten and imprisoned (Jeremiah 20:2; 37:15); Jesus later speaks of the killing of prophets (23:29-37). The disciples stand in their line.

records.source: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἅλας τῆς γῆς· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἁλισθήσεται;
records.gloss: You are the salt of the earth; if but the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be salted?
pieces: You are the salt for the earth. But if salt goes flat, what can give it back its saltiness?

L.13: You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be made salty?

R.13: You are like salt for all the people on earth. But if salt loses its taste, there is no way to make it salty again.

decisions.choice: salt: what gives flavor and keeps food from spoiling
decisions.reason: Salt seasoned food and preserved it. The disciples are what the world needs in order to be what God wants.

decisions.choice: becomes tasteless: loses its saltiness
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "be foolish" or "become tasteless". Salt from the Dead Sea was mixed with other minerals, and the salt could leach out, leaving something that looked like salt but had no taste.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: with what will it be salted?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "nothing". Readable gives the answer.

records.heading: Salt and light

records.source: εἰς οὐδὲν ἰσχύει ἔτι εἰ μὴ βληθὲν ἔξω καταπατεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: For nothing it is strong any longer except having been thrown out to be trampled by the men.
pieces: It is good for nothing anymore but to be thrown out and walked on.

L.13: It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by {{gender:people|men}}.

R.13: It is not good for anything. It gets thrown out, and people walk on it.

decisions.choice: thrown out and trampled: a warning of judgment
decisions.reason: Being thrown out is a picture of rejection at the judgment (8:12; 13:48). Disciples who lose what makes them disciples are useless.

records.source: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου.
records.gloss: You are the light of the world.
pieces: You are the light of the world.

L.14: You are the light of the world.

R.14: You are like a light for the whole world.

decisions.choice: the light of the world: Israel's calling to be a light to the nations
decisions.reason: God called his servant to be "a light for the nations" (Isaiah 42:6; 49:6). Jesus gives that calling to his disciples. In 4:16 Jesus himself is the light.

records.source: οὐ δύναται πόλις κρυβῆναι ἐπάνω ὄρους κειμένη·
records.gloss: Not is able a city to be hidden on a hill lying;
pieces: A town built on a hilltop cannot be hidden.

L.14: A city lying on a hill cannot be hidden.

R.14: Everyone can see a town that is built on top of a hill.

decisions.choice: a city on a hill: seen from far away
decisions.reason: Towns were often built on hills and their white walls could be seen for miles. Some hear an echo of Jerusalem on Mount Zion (Isaiah 2:2-3).

decisions.choice: everyone can see
decisions.reason: Readable says it positively.

records.source: οὐδὲ καίουσιν λύχνον καὶ τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, καὶ λάμπει πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ.
records.gloss: Nor do they light a lamp and put it under the basket, but on the lampstand, and it shines to all the in the house.
pieces: No one lights a lamp and hides it under a basket; it goes on a lampstand, where it shines for everyone in the house.

L.15: Nor do they light a lamp and put it under the basket, but on the lampstand, and it shines for all who [are] in the house.

R.15: People do not light a lamp and then cover it with a bowl. They put it up high on a stand, so it gives light to everyone in the house.

decisions.choice: a lamp under the basket: a small clay oil lamp and a grain measure
decisions.reason: Houses had one room and a small oil lamp. The basket was a measure for grain that held about two gallons; put over the lamp, it would hide the light or put it out.

decisions.choice: No one (B); People (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "they" means people in general.

decisions.choice: a bowl
decisions.reason: Readable names a common container.

records.source: οὕτως λαμψάτω τὸ φῶς ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὅπως ἴδωσιν ὑμῶν τὰ καλὰ ἔργα καὶ δοξάσωσιν τὸν πατέρα ὑμῶν τὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
records.gloss: Thus let shine the light of you before the men, so that they may see of you the good works and may glorify the Father of you the in the heavens.
pieces: In the same way, your light must shine where people can see it, so that they will see your good deeds and give glory to your Father in heaven.

L.16: In the same way let your light shine before {{gender:people|men}}, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who [is] in the heavens.

R.16: In the same way, let your light shine for people to see. Then they will see the good things you do, and they will give glory to your Father in heaven.

decisions.choice: so that they glorify your Father: the good deeds point people to God
alternatives: so that the disciples are praised
decisions.reason: The aim is God's honor, not the disciples' (6:1). The Father in heaven is a name for God that Matthew uses often.

decisions.choice: good works: deeds of mercy and obedience that others can see
decisions.reason: The phrase covers the whole of a life lived as 5:3-12 describes.

decisions.choice: give glory to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the noun form, which keeps the key term.

records.source: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας· οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι·
records.gloss: Not think that I came to abolish the law or the prophets; not I came to abolish but to fulfill;
pieces: Do not suppose that I have come to do away with the law or the prophets. I have not come to do away with them but to fulfill them.

L.17: Do not think that I came to abolish the law or the prophets; I did not come to abolish but to fulfill.

R.17: Do not think that I came to get rid of the law of Moses or the teachings of the prophets. I did not come to get rid of them. I came to make all that they said come true.

decisions.choice: the law or the prophets: the Scriptures
decisions.reason: "The law and the prophets" was a name for the Scriptures (7:12; 22:40).

decisions.choice: fulfill: bring to the full meaning and completion God intended
decisions.reason: In Matthew, Scripture is fulfilled when what it pointed to comes about (1:22; 2:15). Jesus both does what the law and prophets require and brings to completion what they promised; his teaching in 5:21-48 shows the law's full intent.

decisions.choice: the law of Moses, the teachings of the prophets; make all that they said come true
decisions.reason: Readable names the parts of Scripture and gives the main sense of "fulfill".

records.heading: Jesus and the law

records.source: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἕως ἂν παρέλθῃ ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ, ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
records.gloss: Truly for I say to you, until pass away the heaven and the earth, iota one or one stroke not not will pass away from the law until all things happen.
pieces: Truly I tell you, as long as heaven and earth last, not one tiny letter or even part of a letter will vanish from the law until all of it comes about.

L.18: For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke will pass away from the law until all things take place.

R.18: I tell you the truth, as long as heaven and earth last, not even the smallest letter or mark will be taken out of the law. It will stay until everything in it has happened.

decisions.choice: truly: Jesus's solemn "amen" before a saying
alternatives: a response to someone else's words
decisions.reason: "Amen" usually ends a prayer to agree with it. Jesus puts it first to vouch for what he is about to say.

decisions.choice: iota, stroke: the smallest letter and the smallest mark of a letter
decisions.reason: The iota stands for the Hebrew yod, the smallest letter. The stroke is the small hook that tells one Hebrew letter from another.

decisions.choice: until all things take place: until all that the law points to has come about
alternatives: until the end of the world only
decisions.reason: The second "until" can mean the same as the first, or point to what Jesus came to fulfill (5:17).

records.source: ὃς ἐὰν οὖν λύσῃ μίαν τῶν ἐντολῶν τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων καὶ διδάξῃ οὕτως τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ἐλάχιστος κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ποιήσῃ καὶ διδάξῃ, οὗτος μέγας κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν.
records.gloss: Whoever then breaks one of the commandments these the least and teaches thus the men, least will be called in the kingdom of the heavens; whoever but does and teaches, this one great will be called in the kingdom of the heavens.
pieces: So anyone who loosens even the smallest of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But anyone who obeys them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

L.19: So whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches {{gender:people|men}} to do so will be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does [them] and teaches [them], this one will be called great in the kingdom of the heavens.

R.19: So if anyone breaks even the smallest command and teaches other people to do that, that person will be the least important in the kingdom of heaven. But anyone who obeys the commands and teaches others to obey them will be great in the kingdom of heaven.

decisions.choice: breaks: sets aside, treats as not binding
decisions.reason: The verb is related to "abolish" in 5:17. It means loosening a command, by disobeying it or teaching that it does not apply.

decisions.choice: these commandments: the commands of the law, as Jesus interprets them
decisions.reason: "These" points back to the law of 5:17-18. What follows (5:21-48) shows how Jesus reads it.

decisions.choice: least, great: rank within the kingdom
decisions.reason: Both are "in the kingdom". The saying is about standing there, not about entry, which 5:20 takes up.

records.source: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ὑμῶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη πλεῖον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
records.gloss: I say for to you that if not abounds of you the righteousness more [than] the scribes and Pharisees, not not you will enter into the kingdom of the heavens.
pieces: For I tell you, unless your righteousness goes far beyond that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.

L.20: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds [that] of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of the heavens.

R.20: I tell you, you must be more righteous than the teachers of the law and the Pharisees. If you are not, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.

decisions.choice: righteousness: doing God's will
alternatives: a right standing given by God
decisions.reason: As in 5:6 and 5:10, righteousness is a life that does what God requires.

decisions.choice: exceeds the scribes and Pharisees: deeper, from the heart, not more rules
alternatives: more careful keeping of more rules
decisions.reason: The scribes and Pharisees were known for strict keeping of the law. The examples that follow (5:21-48) show a righteousness that reaches to anger, desire, truth and love of enemies (compare 23:23-28).

decisions.choice: the teachers of the law
decisions.reason: As in 2:4, Readable says what the scribes were.

records.source: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐ φονεύσεις· ὃς δ’ ἂν φονεύσῃ, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει.
records.gloss: You heard that it was said to the ancients, Not you will murder; whoever but murders, liable will be to the judgment.
pieces: You have heard what our ancestors were told: 'Do not commit murder. Whoever commits murder must answer for it in court.'

L.21: You have heard that it was said to the ancients, 'You shall not murder; and whoever murders will be liable to the judgment.'

R.21: You have heard that God's law told people long ago, 'Do not murder anyone. Anyone who murders will be judged.'

decisions.choice: it was said to the ancients: the law given to Israel at Sinai, as it was taught
decisions.reason: The dative most likely means "to" the generation at Sinai. The words are the command (Exodus 20:13) and a summary of the penalty (Exodus 21:12), as they were taught and heard in the synagogues.

decisions.choice: liable to the judgment: answerable before a court
decisions.reason: The judgment here is a court that tries cases of murder (Deuteronomy 16:18). Jesus goes on to judgment by God (5:22).

decisions.choice: you have heard ... but I say to you: the pattern of six sayings
decisions.reason: Each of the six sayings (5:21-48) sets the law, or a common reading of it, beside Jesus's own teaching. He goes deeper than the letter, as 5:17-20 says.

decisions.choice: our ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced says whom Jesus's Jewish hearers would understand.

records.heading: Anger

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὀργιζόμενος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει· ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ· Ῥακά, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ· ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ· Μωρέ, ἔνοχος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.
records.gloss: I but say to you that everyone being angry with the brother of him liable will be to the judgment; whoever but says to the brother of him, Raca, liable will be to the council; whoever but says, Fool, liable will be into the Gehenna of the fire.
pieces: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}} will have to answer for it in court. Anyone who says to {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}, 'You empty-head,' will answer to the high council. And anyone who says, 'You fool,' will be in danger of the fire of hell.

L.22: But I say to you that everyone who is angry with {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}} will be liable to the judgment; and whoever says to {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}, 'Raca,' will be liable to the council; and whoever says, 'Fool,' will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.

R.22: But I tell you, if you are angry with {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}, you will be judged. If you insult someone and call them worthless, you will have to stand before the highest court. And if you call someone a fool, you will be in danger of the fire of hell.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow member of God's people, man or woman
decisions.reason: In Matthew "brother" is often a fellow believer or fellow Israelite (18:15, 21; 23:8). The command applies to women as well as men.

decisions.choice: Raca: an Aramaic insult, "empty-head"; fool: one who rejects God
decisions.reason: Raca is an Aramaic word of contempt. "Fool" in Scripture can mean a person without sense or one who denies God (Psalm 14:1). Both treat another person with contempt.

decisions.choice: the council: the Sanhedrin; Gehenna: the place of final judgment by fire
decisions.reason: The Sanhedrin was the highest Jewish court in Jerusalem. Gehenna was the valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem, where children had been sacrificed (Jeremiah 7:31), and its name became a name for the fire of God's judgment.

decisions.choice: the three steps: anger and contempt are as serious as murder before God
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the language of courts in rising order, from the local court to the council to God's judgment, to show that anger itself is under judgment.

decisions.choice: angry with a brother, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: angry with a brother without cause, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "without cause". Early manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: You empty-head (B); call them worthless (R); the fire of hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic word and the place name. Balanced and Readable translate them.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}
decisions.reason: The command covers women and men, so the inclusive form is the default.

records.source: ἐὰν οὖν προσφέρῃς τὸ δῶρόν σου ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κἀκεῖ μνησθῇς ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἔχει τι κατὰ σοῦ, ἄφες ἐκεῖ τὸ δῶρόν σου ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ ὕπαγε πρῶτον διαλλάγηθι τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου, καὶ τότε ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρόν σου.
records.gloss: If therefore you offer the gift of you at the altar and there remember that the brother of you has something against you, \v 24 leave there the gift of you before the altar and go first be reconciled to the brother of you, and then having come offer the gift of you.
pieces: So if you are bringing your offering to the altar and there you remember that {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}} has something against you,
leave your offering there in front of the altar. Go and make peace with {{gender:them|him}} first, and then come back and offer your gift.

L.23: So if you are offering your gift at the altar, and there you remember that {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}} has something against you,
L.24: leave your gift there before the altar and go, first be reconciled to {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}}, and then come and offer your gift.

R.23: So suppose you are about to give your gift to God at the altar in the temple. Then you remember that {{gender:a brother or sister|a brother}} is upset with you because of something you did.
R.24: Leave your gift there by the altar. Go and make things right with {{gender:that person|him}} first. Then come back and give your gift to God.

decisions.choice: your gift at the altar: an offering brought to the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The gift is a sacrifice given to a priest at the altar of the temple. Galileans had a journey of several days to reach it, which sharpens the command to go back first.

decisions.choice: has something against you: has a grievance because you wronged them
decisions.reason: The one who comes to worship is the one at fault. Being reconciled matters more to God than the offering (Hosea 6:6, quoted in 9:13).

decisions.choice: make peace with (B); make things right with (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for reconciliation.

decisions.choice: the altar in the temple; give your gift to God
decisions.reason: Readable says where the altar was and to whom the gift is given.

records.source: ἴσθι εὐνοῶν τῷ ἀντιδίκῳ σου ταχὺ ἕως ὅτου εἶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, μήποτέ σε παραδῷ ὁ ἀντίδικος τῷ κριτῇ, καὶ ὁ κριτὴς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ, καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν βληθήσῃ·
records.gloss: Be agreeing with the opponent of you quickly while you are with him on the way, lest you hand over the opponent to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and into prison you will be thrown;
pieces: If someone is taking you to court, settle with {{gender:them|him}} quickly while you are still on the way there. Otherwise your accuser may hand you over to the judge, the judge may hand you over to the guard, and you may be thrown into prison.

L.25: Come to terms quickly with your opponent while you are on the way with {{gender:them|him}}, lest the opponent hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.

R.25: Suppose someone is taking you to court. Make things right with that person quickly, before you get there. If you do not, that person may take you to the judge. The judge may give you to the guard, and you will be put in prison.

decisions.choice: your opponent: someone taking you to court, probably over a debt
decisions.reason: The word is a legal one. Prison for debt kept a person until the debt was paid (18:30).

decisions.choice: a picture of the coming judgment as well as everyday advice
decisions.reason: The saying is sound advice in itself, but placed after 5:22 it also warns that there is little time to be reconciled before God's judgment.

decisions.choice: the situation first, then the advice
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set out the case before saying what to do.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως ἂν ἀποδῷς τὸν ἔσχατον κοδράντην.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you, not not you will come out from there until you pay the last quadrans.
pieces: Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid {{units:the last penny|the last quadrans}}.

L.26: Truly I tell you, you will never get out of there until you have paid the last quadrans.

R.26: I tell you the truth, you will not get out until you have paid {{units:every last cent|the last quadrans}}.

decisions.choice: quadrans: the smallest Roman coin
decisions.reason: A quadrans was a quarter of a copper as, a sixty-fourth of a denarius, which was a day's wage for a laborer. The debt must be paid in full.

decisions.choice: {{units:the last penny|the last quadrans}} (B); {{units:every last cent|the last quadrans}} (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the modern smallest coin by default, with the original coin as the alternative. Literal keeps the original coin.

records.source: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις.
records.gloss: You heard that it was said, Not you will commit adultery.
pieces: You have heard the commandment, 'Do not commit adultery.'

L.27: You have heard that it was said, 'You shall not commit adultery.'

R.27: You have heard that the law says, 'Do not commit adultery.' That means do not be unfaithful to your husband or wife.

decisions.choice: You shall not commit adultery: the seventh commandment (Exodus 20:14)
decisions.reason: The command forbade sexual relations with another person's spouse (Deuteronomy 5:18).

decisions.choice: That means do not be unfaithful to your husband or wife.
decisions.reason: Readable says what adultery is.

records.heading: Adultery

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ βλέπων γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτὴν ἤδη ἐμοίχευσεν αὐτὴν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: I but say to you that everyone looking at a woman in order to desire her already committed adultery [with] her in the heart of him.
pieces: But I tell you, a man who looks at a woman with the aim of wanting her for himself has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

L.28: But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman in order to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

R.28: But I tell you, if a man looks at a woman and wants to have sex with her, he has already sinned with her in his heart. It is the same as adultery.

decisions.choice: in order to desire her: looking with the purpose of wanting her sexually
alternatives: noticing that a woman is attractive
decisions.reason: The construction states a purpose. The verb is the one used in the command against coveting a neighbor's wife (Exodus 20:17 in the Greek Old Testament).

decisions.choice: in his heart: in his inner self, where intentions are formed
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is the center of thought and will. Sin begins there before it is done (15:19).

decisions.choice: everyone who looks: a man, as the following "his heart" shows
decisions.reason: The saying is put in terms of a man looking at a woman, the case the commandment has in view. The principle applies to all.

decisions.choice: a man who (B); if a man (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that the saying is about a man; it takes no gender setting.

records.source: εἰ δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου βληθῇ εἰς γέενναν.
records.gloss: If but the eye of you the right causes to stumble you, tear out it and throw from you; it is better for you that perishes one of the members of you and not whole the body of you be thrown into Gehenna.
pieces: If your right eye leads you into sin, pull it out and get rid of it. You are better off losing one part of your body than having all of you thrown into hell.

L.29: And if your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw [it] away from you, for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.

R.29: If your right eye makes you sin, pull it out and throw it away. It is better to lose one part of your body than to have your whole body thrown into hell.

decisions.choice: tear out, cut off: overstatement that demands drastic action against sin
alternatives: a command to harm the body
decisions.reason: Jesus uses deliberate overstatement, as teachers of the time did. Removing an eye would not stop desire, which comes from the heart (5:28; 15:19). The point is to deal ruthlessly with whatever leads to sin, because the stakes are eternal.

decisions.choice: causes you to stumble: leads you into sin
decisions.reason: The verb pictures a trap or a stone that trips someone. Here it means leading into sin that ruins a person.

decisions.choice: the right eye: the one thought more valuable
decisions.reason: The right eye and the right hand (5:30) were thought the better ones. Even what is most valued must go.

decisions.choice: Gehenna (L); hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name, explained at 5:22. Balanced and Readable use the English word for the place of final judgment.

decisions.choice: leads you into sin (B); makes you sin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means.

records.source: καὶ εἰ ἡ δεξιά σου χεὶρ σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὴν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου εἰς γέενναν ἀπέλθῃ.
records.gloss: And if the right of you hand causes to stumble you, cut off it and throw from you; it is better for you that perishes one of the members of you and not whole the body of you into Gehenna go away.
pieces: And if your right hand leads you into sin, cut it off and get rid of it. You are better off losing one part of your body than having all of you go into hell.

L.30: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw [it] away from you, for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go into Gehenna.

R.30: If your right hand makes you sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to go to hell.

decisions.choice: tear out, cut off: overstatement that demands drastic action against sin
alternatives: a command to harm the body
decisions.reason: Jesus uses deliberate overstatement, as teachers of the time did. Removing an eye would not stop desire, which comes from the heart (5:28; 15:19). The point is to deal ruthlessly with whatever leads to sin, because the stakes are eternal.

decisions.choice: Gehenna (L); hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name, explained at 5:22. Balanced and Readable use the English word for the place of final judgment.

decisions.choice: leads you into sin (B); makes you sin (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:29.

records.source: Ἐρρέθη δέ· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, δότω αὐτῇ ἀποστάσιον.
records.gloss: It was said also, Whoever divorces the wife of him, let him give to her a certificate of divorce.
pieces: It was also said, 'A man who sends his wife away must give her a written notice of divorce.'

L.31: And it was said, 'Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.'

R.31: The law also says, 'If a man divorces his wife, he must give her a paper that says she is divorced.'

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 24:1-4: the written notice of divorce
decisions.reason: The law took divorce for granted and regulated it: a husband who sent his wife away had to give her a written document, which left her free to marry again.

decisions.choice: divorces: in Jewish law only the husband could divorce
decisions.reason: Teachers of the time disagreed over the grounds. Some allowed divorce only for sexual unfaithfulness, others for almost any cause (19:3).

records.heading: Divorce

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι, καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσῃ μοιχᾶται.
records.gloss: I but say to you that everyone divorcing the wife of him except on account of sexual immorality makes her to commit adultery, and whoever a divorced [woman] marries commits adultery.
pieces: But I tell you that a man who divorces his wife for any reason other than sexual unfaithfulness causes her to commit adultery, and anyone who marries a woman who has been divorced commits adultery.

L.32: But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

R.32: But I tell you, if a man divorces his wife for any reason except sexual unfaithfulness, he causes her to commit adultery if she marries again. And any man who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: sexual unfaithfulness by the wife
decisions.reason: The word covers sexual sin of many kinds. In a saying about marriage it most likely means the wife's unfaithfulness. Others limit it to marriages the law forbade (Leviticus 18) or to unfaithfulness during betrothal (as in 1:19).

decisions.choice: makes her commit adultery: when she marries again, as she would be expected to
alternatives: makes her an adulteress at the moment of divorce
decisions.reason: A divorced woman with no means of support would usually remarry. Since in God's sight the first marriage still stands, that marriage is adultery, and the husband who divorced her bears the blame.

decisions.choice: if she marries again
decisions.reason: Readable states the assumption the saying makes.

records.source: Πάλιν ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις, ἀποδώσεις δὲ τῷ κυρίῳ τοὺς ὅρκους σου.
records.gloss: Again you heard that it was said to the ancients, Not you will swear falsely, you will pay but to the Lord the oaths of you.
pieces: You have also heard what our ancestors were told: 'Do not swear falsely. Do what you have promised the Lord with an oath.'

L.33: Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, 'You shall not swear falsely, but you shall carry out your oaths to the Lord.'

R.33: You have also heard that people long ago were told, 'Do not make a promise to God and then break it. Do what you promised the Lord.'

decisions.choice: Leviticus 19:12; Numbers 30:2; Deuteronomy 23:21
decisions.reason: The words sum up several laws: do not swear falsely by God's name, and keep the vows you make to him.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew of these laws
decisions.reason: As in 4:7 and 4:10.

decisions.choice: swear falsely: break an oath, or swear to what is untrue
decisions.reason: An oath called on God as witness. The verb covers both false oaths and broken ones.

decisions.choice: our ancestors
decisions.reason: As in 5:21.

records.heading: Oaths

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ὀμόσαι ὅλως· μήτε ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὅτι θρόνος ἐστὶν τοῦ θεοῦ·
records.gloss: I but say to you not to swear at all; neither by the heaven, because throne it is of the God;
pieces: But I tell you, do not take an oath at all, not by heaven, because it is God's throne,

L.34: But I say to you not to swear at all: neither by heaven, because it is [the] throne of God,

R.34: But I tell you, never make a promise by swearing an oath. Do not swear by heaven, because heaven is where God rules as king.

decisions.choice: not to swear at all: no oaths to guarantee your words
alternatives: no oaths in a law court
decisions.reason: Jesus forbids the oaths people used to make their words believed. Where every word is true, no oath is needed (5:37). Christians have differed over whether this rules out oaths required by a court.

decisions.choice: heaven is God's throne: Isaiah 66:1
decisions.reason: God says, "Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool." To swear by heaven is still to swear by God (23:22).

decisions.choice: where God rules as king
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of a throne.

records.source: μήτε ἐν τῇ γῇ, ὅτι ὑποπόδιόν ἐστιν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· μήτε εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὅτι πόλις ἐστὶν τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως·
records.gloss: nor by the earth, because footstool it is of the feet of him; nor to Jerusalem, because city it is of the great King;
pieces: or by the earth, because it is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} footstool, or by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King.

L.35: nor by the earth, because it is [the] footstool of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, nor by Jerusalem, because it is [the] city of the great King,

R.35: Do not swear by the earth, because it belongs to God. It is where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rests {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet. Do not swear by Jerusalem, because it is the city of God, the great King.

decisions.choice: footstool: Isaiah 66:1; city of the great King: Psalm 48:3
decisions.reason: The earth and Jerusalem belong to God as much as heaven does. People swore by them to avoid naming God, but every such oath still calls on him.

decisions.choice: it belongs to God; the city of God, the great King
alternatives: his footstool; the city of the great King
decisions.reason: Readable says that each picture speaks of God.

records.source: μήτε ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ σου ὀμόσῃς, ὅτι οὐ δύνασαι μίαν τρίχα λευκὴν ποιῆσαι ἢ μέλαιναν.
records.gloss: Nor by the head of you swear, because not you are able one hair white to make or black.
pieces: Do not swear by your own head either, since you cannot turn a single hair white or black.

L.36: Nor shall you swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black.

R.36: Do not even swear by your own head. You cannot make one hair on it white or black.

decisions.choice: you cannot make one hair white or black: even your own life is in God's hands
decisions.reason: To swear by one's head was to pledge one's life. But a person does not control even the color of a hair; life belongs to God.

records.source: ἔστω δὲ ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν ναὶ ναί, οὒ οὔ· τὸ δὲ περισσὸν τούτων ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἐστιν.
records.gloss: Let be but the word of you yes yes, no no; the but more of these from the evil is.
pieces: Let your yes be yes and your no be no. Whatever you add to that comes from the evil one.

L.37: But let your word be 'Yes, yes,' 'No, no'; and what is more than these is from the evil one.

R.37: When you say yes, mean yes. When you say no, mean no. If you say more than that, it comes from the evil one.

decisions.choice: yes, yes; no, no: a plain yes or no that can be trusted
alternatives: a double yes as a kind of oath
decisions.reason: The doubled words stress that a yes should mean yes and a no mean no (compare James 5:12).

decisions.choice: the evil one: the devil
decisions.reason: The form can be masculine (the evil one) or neuter (evil). Matthew uses the masculine of the devil in 13:19 and 13:38, and the need for oaths comes from a world where lying is common.

records.source: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ὀφθαλμὸν ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ὀδόντα ἀντὶ ὀδόντος.
records.gloss: You heard that it was said, Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.
pieces: You have heard the saying, 'Eye for eye, tooth for tooth.'

L.38: You have heard that it was said, 'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.'

R.38: You have heard that the law says, 'The punishment must match the harm: an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.'

decisions.choice: eye for eye: the law of equal justice (Exodus 21:24; Leviticus 24:20; Deuteronomy 19:21)
decisions.reason: The law set a limit for judges: the penalty must match the harm and go no further. In practice it was often settled by payment. People could also take it as a right to pay back what they had suffered.

decisions.choice: The punishment must match the harm
decisions.reason: Readable says what the principle meant.

records.heading: Do not take revenge

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ἀντιστῆναι τῷ πονηρῷ· ἀλλ’ ὅστις σε ῥαπίζει εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην·
records.gloss: I but say to you not to resist the evil [person]; but whoever you strikes on the right cheek, turn to him also the other;
pieces: But I tell you, do not fight back against an evil person. If anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn the other cheek to {{gender:them|him}} as well.

L.39: But I say to you not to resist the evil [person]; but whoever strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other to {{gender:them|him}} as well,

R.39: But I tell you, do not fight back against someone who does wrong to you. If someone slaps you on the right side of your face, let them slap the other side too.

decisions.choice: do not resist the evil person: do not pay back wrong with wrong
alternatives: never oppose evil in any way
decisions.reason: After "eye for eye", resisting means taking revenge or answering harm with harm. The examples are of insults and demands made on a person, not of standing by while others are harmed.

decisions.choice: slaps you on the right cheek: a backhanded slap, an insult
decisions.reason: A right-handed blow to the right cheek would be with the back of the hand, a gesture of contempt. The point is not to answer insult with insult.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The one who strikes may be anyone, so the inclusive form is the default. Readable uses "someone ... them", which already includes everyone.

records.source: καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον·
records.gloss: and to the [one] wanting you to sue and the tunic of you to take, let go to him also the cloak;
pieces: If someone wants to take you to court and take your shirt, let {{gender:them|him}} have your coat as well.

L.40: and to the one who wants to sue you and take your tunic, let {{gender:them|him}} have your cloak as well,

R.40: If someone takes you to court to get your shirt, give that person your coat too.

decisions.choice: tunic and cloak: the inner garment and the outer one
decisions.reason: The tunic was worn next to the skin; the cloak was the outer garment, also used as a blanket at night. The law did not let a creditor keep a poor man's cloak overnight (Exodus 22:26-27). Jesus tells his followers to give up even what the law protected.

decisions.choice: shirt, coat
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the nearest modern garments; Literal keeps the ancient names.

records.source: καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετ’ αὐτοῦ δύο.
records.gloss: and whoever you will compel mile one, go with him two.
pieces: If someone forces you to carry a load one mile, go two miles with {{gender:them|him}}.

L.41: and whoever compels you to go one mile, go with {{gender:them|him}} two.

R.41: If a soldier makes you carry something for one mile, carry it two miles.

decisions.choice: compels: forces you into service, as Roman soldiers could
decisions.reason: The verb is a borrowed word for official forced service. Soldiers and officials could make people carry loads, as Simon of Cyrene was made to carry the cross (27:32).

decisions.choice: mile: a Roman mile, a thousand paces, a little shorter than a modern mile
decisions.reason: The difference does not affect the saying.

decisions.choice: to carry a load (B); a soldier makes you carry something (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says what was usually demanded; Readable names who usually demanded it. The Greek does not name the person.

records.source: τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.
records.gloss: To the [one] asking you give, and the [one] wanting from you to borrow not you turn away.
pieces: Give to anyone who asks you, and do not turn your back on someone who wants to borrow from you.

L.42: To the one who asks you, give, and the one who wants to borrow from you, do not turn away.

R.42: Give to anyone who asks you for something. And do not refuse to lend to anyone who wants to borrow from you.

decisions.choice: give and lend: the generosity the law asked for (Deuteronomy 15:7-11)
alternatives: a rule to give whatever is asked
decisions.reason: The law told Israel to lend freely to the poor. Jesus's saying belongs with the others: a disciple does not hold on to his rights or his goods.

records.source: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου καὶ μισήσεις τὸν ἐχθρόν σου.
records.gloss: You heard that it was said, You will love the neighbor of you and will hate the enemy of you.
pieces: You have heard the saying, 'Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'

L.43: You have heard that it was said, 'You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'

R.43: You have heard that people say, 'Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'

decisions.choice: love your neighbor: Leviticus 19:18; hate your enemy: not in the law
alternatives: both halves are commands of the law
decisions.reason: The law commands love of neighbor. No law commands hatred of enemies, but it was drawn from the first command: if the neighbor is a fellow Israelite, the enemy is not. The Dead Sea Scrolls teach hatred of the "sons of darkness" (Rule of the Community 1.10).

decisions.choice: people say
decisions.reason: The second half is not in the law, so Readable does not say "the law says" here.

records.heading: Love your enemies

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς·
records.gloss: I but say to you, love the enemies of you and pray for the [ones] persecuting you;
pieces: But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for the people who persecute you,

L.44: But I say to you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,

R.44: But I tell you, love your enemies. Pray for the people who hurt you.

decisions.choice: love: seek their good, whatever you feel
decisions.reason: The command is to act for the good of enemies and to pray for them, as God does good to all (5:45).

decisions.choice: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: with "bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you" added, from Luke 6:27-28, in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts fill out the verse with words from Luke. Early manuscripts have the shorter text. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

records.source: ὅπως γένησθε υἱοὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, ὅτι τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ πονηροὺς καὶ ἀγαθοὺς καὶ βρέχει ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ἀδίκους.
records.gloss: so that you may become sons of the Father of you the in heavens, because the sun of him he makes rise on evil and good and sends rain on righteous and unrighteous.
pieces: so that you will be {{gender:children|sons}} of your Father in heaven. He makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sun rise on evil people and good people alike, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends rain on those who do right and those who do wrong.

L.45: so that you may become {{gender:children|sons}} of your Father who [is] in [the] heavens, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sun rise on [the] evil and [the] good, and sends rain on [the] righteous and [the] unrighteous.

R.45: Then you will show that you are {{gender:children|sons}} of your Father in heaven. He makes the sun shine on bad people and good people. He sends rain to people who do right and to people who do wrong.

decisions.choice: become sons of your Father: be like him, and so show you are his children
alternatives: earn the right to be his children
decisions.reason: A son was expected to be like his father. Those who love their enemies act as God does, and so show the family likeness (5:9).

decisions.choice: his sun and his rain for all: God's kindness to good and bad alike
decisions.reason: God gives the gifts of life to everyone, including those who oppose him. His children are to love in the same way.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: As in 5:9.

decisions.choice: you will show that you are
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "become" here: being seen to be what they are.

records.source: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀγαπήσητε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, τίνα μισθὸν ἔχετε;
records.gloss: If for you love the [ones] loving you, what reward do you have?
pieces: If you love the people who love you, what reward is there in that?

L.46: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have?

R.46: If you love only the people who love you, why should God reward you for that?

decisions.choice: what reward: such love deserves nothing special from God
alternatives: no reward at all for any love
decisions.reason: Love that only returns love is ordinary. The reward belongs to love that goes beyond it (5:12; 6:1).

decisions.choice: only; why should God reward you
alternatives: those who love you; what reward do you have
decisions.reason: Readable makes the contrast and the giver of the reward plain.

records.source: οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ τελῶναι τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
records.gloss: Not also the tax collectors the same do?
pieces: Even tax collectors do that, do they not?

L.46: Do not even the tax collectors do the same?

decisions.choice: tax collectors: Jews who collected taxes and tolls for Rome or for Herod's family
decisions.reason: They were despised as collaborators and cheats, and named alongside sinners (9:10-11). Even they are loyal to their own.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes; Readable gives the answer.

records.source: καὶ ἐὰν ἀσπάσησθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὑμῶν μόνον, τί περισσὸν ποιεῖτε;
records.gloss: And if you greet the brothers of you only, what more do you do?
pieces: And if you greet only your own {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, what are you doing that is out of the ordinary?

L.47: And if you greet only your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, what more are you doing?

R.47: If you are friendly only to your own family and friends, you are doing nothing more than anyone else.

decisions.choice: greet: wish peace to someone, a sign of goodwill
decisions.reason: A greeting wished God's peace on the other person and treated them as one of your own (10:12-13).

decisions.choice: brothers: your own people, those of your own group, men and women
friendly only to your own family and friends
decisions.reason: Readable says what greeting showed and who "brothers" are here.

records.source: οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ ἐθνικοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
records.gloss: Not also the Gentiles the same do?
pieces: Even the Gentiles do that, do they not?

L.47: Do not even the Gentiles do the same?

R.47: Even people who do not know God do that!

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: people outside Israel who did not worship its God
decisions.reason: The word here describes outsiders whose ways are not God's ways (6:7, 32; 18:17).

decisions.choice: people who do not know God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word and gives the answer the question expects.

records.source: Ἔσεσθε οὖν ὑμεῖς τέλειοι ὡς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τέλειός ἐστιν.
records.gloss: You will be therefore you perfect as the Father of you the heavenly perfect is.
pieces: You, then, are to be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

L.48: You therefore shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

R.48: So you must be perfect, the way your Father in heaven is perfect.

decisions.choice: perfect: complete, whole, undivided, here above all in love
decisions.reason: The word means complete or whole. After 5:43-47 it means love that is whole, like God's, which leaves no one out. It echoes "You shall be holy, for I am holy" (Leviticus 19:2) and "You shall be blameless" (Deuteronomy 18:13).

decisions.choice: you shall be: a command in the form of a future
decisions.reason: As often in the law, the future tense gives a command.
